title: Nucleation and time-reversal symmetry breaking in nonconserved scalar field theories
authors: Noah Ziethen, Michalis Chatzittofi, Michael E. Cates, Cesare Nardini
abstract: Classical nucleation theory (CNT) describes the formation of a stable phase from a metastable one in terms of a single reaction coordinate that corresponds to the radius of a nucleating droplet. In this work, we provide a full account of nonequilibrium nucleation theory (NNT), which generalizes CNT to non-equilibrium field theories with non-conserved order parameter. We present two equivalent derivations of the dynamics of the droplet radius: a stochastic route, based on a direct projection of the stochastic field equation onto the radial reaction coordinate, and a route based on the minimization of the Freidlin-Wentzell action. Crucially, the quasipotential barrier predicted by NNT differs from the one found when assuming the instanton to be the time-reversal of the relaxation dynamics. Whereas the interfacial density profile differs from that on the relaxation path, an analytical derivation of NNT remains possible using a careful definition of the reaction coordinate. This leverages the perturbative structure that (in common with CNT) emerges in the limit of large critical radius. We further derive with similar techniques the dynamics of capillary waves, whose stability is required for the CNT/NNT precept of a near-spherical droplet to prevail. After deriving our theory for generic non-conserved field-theories, we address two explicit examples: a non-equilibrium generalization of Model A (Active Model A), and a population dynamics model (with two choices of noise that each break time-reversal symmetry). In both cases, we validate our analytical NNT against numerical results obtained by action minimization, with excellent agreement. NNT provide a systematic framework for constructing nucleation theories in a broad class of non-equilibrium systems from active matter, reaction-diffusion systems and population dynamics.
summary: This paper develops Nonequilibrium Nucleation Theory (NNT) to describe phase transitions in fluctuating, non-conserved field theories beyond the scope of classical theory. It rigorously derives the dynamics by comparing stochastic projection methods with action minimization techniques. The work establishes a systematic framework for calculating nucleation rates in complex systems like active matter, emphasizing when and how time-reversal symmetry breaks down.
main_problem: The work aims to provide a full, rigorous account of Nonequilibrium Nucleation Theory (NNT), generalizing Classical Nucleation Theory (CNT) for systems where the order parameter is non-conserved.
main_result: NNT provides a systematic framework that correctly predicts the quasipotential barrier in non-equilibrium settings, differing from assumptions based on time-reversal symmetry. The theory was successfully validated against numerical simulations for active matter and population dynamics models.
method: The authors employ two equivalent derivations: projecting the stochastic field equation onto the reaction coordinate (stochastic route) and minimizing the Freidlin-Wentzell action (action route).
model_or_system: The theory applies to nonconserved scalar field theories, modeled by stochastic differential equations $\partial_t \phi = -\mu[\phi] + \sqrt{D(\phi)}\xi$. Examples include Active Model A and population dynamics models.
key_observables: Nucleation rate ($P$), quasipotential barrier height, critical radius ($R_c$), and the droplet radius ($R$) acting as the reaction coordinate.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($T$), mobility ($M(R)$), and the functional form of the drift ($\mu[\phi]$) and noise amplitude ($D(\phi)$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that a careful definition of the reaction coordinate allows for an analytical derivation, although it explicitly notes that assuming time-reversal symmetry (TRR) can lead to incorrect results for mobility and quasipotential in non-equilibrium cases.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates nucleation dynamics, showing droplet formation, density profiles versus radial coordinates, and the functional integral used to define the critical radius $R$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces NNT as a generalization of CNT. It then presents two derivations for the droplet dynamics (stochastic vs. action minimization), highlighting discrepancies when TRR is assumed. Finally, it applies the theory to concrete examples like Active Model A and population dynamics models.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous treatment of non-equilibrium fluctuations and rare events using path integrals and large deviation theory has methodological overlaps with open quantum systems where dissipation and noise are key. The systematic framework for deriving effective potentials in non-equilibrium settings is valuable.
